I'm not sure `freeConnectionsCounter` represents idle open connections. In Redisson it tracks available permits/capacity, while actual idle connections are kept separately in `freeConnections`. For example, in Redisson 3.17.7, acquiring/releasing a connection updates `freeConnectionsCounter`, while idle connections are added/polled from `freeConnections` separately: https://github.com/redisson/redisson/blob/redisson-3.17.7/redisson/src/main/java/org/redisson/connection/ClientConnectionsEntry.java#L148-L184

Redisson's own idle cleanup logic also combines both values (`maximumAmount - freeConnectionsCounter.getCounter() + connections.size()`): https://github.com/redisson/redisson/blob/redisson-3.17.7/redisson/src/main/java/org/redisson/connection/IdleConnectionWatcher.java#L99-L100

This means recording `freeConnectionsCounter` as the `idle` connection count can report unopened capacity as idle open connections, e.g. a max-64 pool can look like it has 64 idle connections even when few/no connections have actually been opened. Can we record actual idle/open counts instead, or omit the usage metric if Redisson doesn't expose those reliably across this version range?

```suggestion
public class RedissonConnectionPoolMetrics {
```
Repo style: don't add `final` to classes in `javaagent/src/main/`.

The reflective path is only exercised at the two ends of the range: `test` runs 2.3.0 (`AtomicInteger`, no reflection) and `latestDepTest` runs 3.17.+. Everything in between is untested, and `AsyncSemaphore`'s internals change several times:

| Version | `counter` | `listeners` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2.5.x | `int` | `Queue<Runnable>` (`LinkedList`) |
| 3.5 - 3.11 | `int` / `volatile int` | `Set<Entry>` (`LinkedHashSet`) |
| 3.16.3 | `AtomicInteger` | `Queue<Runnable>` |
| 3.17.x | `AtomicInteger` | `Queue<CompletableFuture>` |

Could you add a `JvmTestSuite` pinned to a mid version (e.g. 3.11.x) to cover the `int counter` + `LinkedHashSet listeners` shape? Same pattern as `jsf-mojarra-1.2`.

One thing to note for that range: both fields are mutated under `synchronized (this)` and `counter` isn't always volatile, so reading them reflectively has no visibility guarantee.
Returning 0 on failure means `used = maxConnections - 0`, so the pool reports as fully saturated. Better to signal failure and skip recording than to report a wrong value.

`Collection.size()` is never negative.

`RedisClient` doesn't override `equals`/`hashCode` in 2.3.0 or 3.17.7, so `ConcurrentHashMap<RedisClient, BatchCallback>` already gives identity semantics. `TomcatConnectionPoolMetrics` does exactly this with a comment explaining why.
The subscription pool (args 3/4 and `freeSubscribeConnections`) is ignored, and the pool name doesn't distinguish. Is that intentional?

[General] This is more than a test expectation — the instrumentation emits a wrong value here. `SingleEntry.setupMasterEntry()` passes `getSlaveConnectionMinimumIdleSize()` as the constructor's `subscribePoolMinSize`, so `db.client.connection.idle.min` for the *subscription* pool reports the *regular* pool's minimum (5) rather than the configured `subscriptionConnectionMinimumIdleSize` (2). Nothing in the exported metric tells a user it's wrong.

Worth flagging that raising `minVersion` won't fix it: the 3.x line forked before the fix and reintroduced the same bug, so no single floor covers it (it was fixed in 2.8.1, then again in 3.3.1).

The correct value is recoverable, though. Constructor argument 5 is the `ConnectionManager`, and `ConnectionManager.getConfig()` is stable across 2.3.0–3.17.x; in single-server mode `SingleConnectionManager` copies the user's setting into that config, so it holds the right value on exactly the affected path. Reading it there needs **no version detection** — the non-buggy paths pass precisely this config value, so the same read is correct on every version:

- add `@Advice.Argument(5) Object connectionManager` to the advice and thread it through to `registerSubscriptionMetrics`
- resolve `getConfig()` reflectively, then the min-idle getter, trying `getSubscriptionConnectionMinimumIdleSize` and falling back to `getSlaveSubscriptionConnectionMinimumIdleSize` (2.3.0 only has the latter, 3.17.x only the former, versions in between have both; the declaring class is public, so no `setAccessible` is needed)
- fall back to the `subscriptionPoolMinSize` argument if any lookup fails
- only apply the override where a subscription pool is actually registered — 2.3.0 master entries in master/slave mode pass `0, 0`, and those shouldn't gain a synthetic minimum

That is structurally the same shape as the `AsyncSemaphoreAccessor` this PR already ships, so it adds no new *kind* of complexity — and it lets this test assert the configured value unconditionally instead of encoding the bug.

Redisson has no max-idle setting, so this makes `db.client.connection.idle.max` an exact copy of `db.client.connection.max` for every pool. The other pool instrumentations here whose library lacks the concept (HikariCP, c3p0, Oracle UCP, Vibur) just don't emit the instrument at all; only Druid and Tomcat JDBC do, and both have a real `getMaxIdle()`.

I'd drop `maxIdleConnections` from the batch callback and remove the matching `db.client.connection.idle.max` assertion in the test, rather than publishing a duplicated series.

`listeners.size()` isn't the pending count across the whole supported range. In 3.13.6 through 3.15.x, `AsyncSemaphore.remove()` doesn't remove anything from `listeners` — it parks the listener in a separate `removedListeners` set, and Redisson's own `queueSize()` returns `listeners.size() - removedListeners.size()`. `ClientConnectionsEntry.removeConnection()` calls that on acquire timeout, so on those versions pending_requests reads high and stays high until the stale entry is polled.

`queueSize()` is public from 3.4 onward (it's missing in 3.2, which is presumably why you went to the field). Resolving it reflectively and only falling back to the `listeners` field for the older versions would match Redisson's own accounting everywhere.

@YaoYingLong Could we start with the current versions instead, and come back to this older range later? 3.26 through the current 4.6.1 is one stable shape (`ConnectionsHolder`), and it exposes the connection lists as public methods -- so no reflection, and real open/idle counts instead of permit arithmetic. That would also settle the idle/used question from my first review, which this range can't really answer: `getAllConnections()` only became public in 3.9.0, and compiling against 2.3.0 puts it out of reach for everything.

The old versions are worth covering eventually, but doing them second means they can follow the newer module's semantics rather than the other way around. Also, not sure 3.18 is really a boundary -- the `ClientConnectionsEntry` constructor is unchanged there, it's just the `AsyncSemaphore` package move. The real breaks appear to be 3.20 and 3.26.

replies.body: Sounds good. The implementation for the current version is complete, so I'll create a PR for the current version first.

[General] Redisson 3.15.6 can return `-1` while `tryRun()` polls a canceled listener before removing it from `removedListeners`. Clamp the value so the callback does not export an impossible pending-request count.

```suggestion
              pending.record(Math.max(0, pendingRequests), attributes);
```

[Javaagent] This name-only type matcher is already a cheap class-name check, so the prefilter adds a second lookup without avoiding bytecode inspection. Repository guidance reserves `classLoaderOptimization()` for hierarchy or annotation matchers; please remove this override and its import.

[Testing] None of these suites exercises the `listeners`-field fallback: 2.3 uses `AtomicInteger`, while 3.11 and later expose `queueSize()`. Please add an early `AsyncSemaphore` suite such as 2.5.1, where pending requests depend on reflecting `listeners`.

[Style] This class and its two public supplier methods are used only from the same `v2_3` package; `getSubscriptionMinimumIdleSize` already uses package visibility. Please make all three package-private per the least-access rule.
how would you get a `RuntimeException` here?

replies.body: There isn't a reachable RuntimeException on the supported path. counterField is resolved from AsyncSemaphore itself, and this supplier is only created for an AsyncSemaphore instance. Across the supported versions the field is either int (boxed as Integer) or AtomicInteger. I'll remove RuntimeException here and only handle IllegalAccessException.

threads.body: is this for suppressing security exceptions?

replies.body: Yes. Class.getMethod () documents SecurityException when package access is denied. I'll narrow this catch to SecurityException so the best-effort lookup does not suppress unrelated runtime failures.
